founding_year.basis: Founded 1995 by Bob Kagle, Bruce Dunlevie, Andy Rachleff, Kevin Harvey and Val Vaden. Corroborated by the fund ladder: Benchmark Capital Partners L.P. (CIK 1031285) filed its first 13G in February 1998.

aum.basis: Benchmark Capital Holdings Co. LLC is an EXEMPT REPORTING ADVISER (SEC 802-75842, CRD 160352, ERA since 2012-03-30), not a registered investment adviser, so no Item 5.F regulatory AUM exists. The sworn substitute is Schedule D Section 7.B.(1): 34 private funds whose current gross asset values sum to $7,582,538,663 on the annual amendment filed 2026-03-24 (parsed at run time by scratch/own-formd-persons.py's sibling ADV pass). Both range ends are the same sworn number because no credible press figure sits above it. ONE CAVEAT WORTH RECORDING: Benchmark names its funds in Section 7.B by NUMERIC CODE ('1094', '2165', '2645' …) under rule 204-2(d), which permits an adviser to preserve a fund client's anonymity, so the gross asset values cannot be mapped to named funds — the composite is sound, the per-fund attribution is not available, and the fund table below is built from Form D instead.

funds.basis: The flagship ladder plus the two 2026 vehicles and the Cerebras pair. FILING STYLE MATTERS HERE and it is the opposite of Lightspeed's: Benchmark files the FULL fund size as the Form D total-offering amount at or before first close, so the offering is the fund size and the sold amount is the close state on the filing date — Fund VII shows $5M sold against a $425M offering, Fund IX $0 against $425M. Sizes are therefore the offering amounts, asserted against the accessions. Funds I, II, IV, V and VI (1995-2008) predate electronic Form D and carry no sworn size; the firm held every flagship at roughly $425M from 2011 to 2024. The 18 Founders' Fund co-invest vehicles, the Management Co. GPs and the WS SPV are counted in the base's evidence but not listed as funds — they are employee co-invest and GP plumbing, not capital raised from LPs.

investment_stage.basis: DERIVED, not taken from a site — the firm publishes no positioning. Series A is the core: 243 of 284 base rows. Seed is real but small (11 rows, including the LangChain and Legora seeds). Growth became a declared strategy in June 2026 with Benchmark Partners T1 ($1.25B, the firm's first dedicated late-stage fund, five to six large positions) and was already visible in the base as 29 Growth entries, mostly Series B or later entries at scale.

investment_geo.basis: 260 of 284 base rows are US. The two 'other' labels are the firm's own historical desks rather than a current mandate: the taxonomy caps the core at two labels and there is only one core here. Non-US rows outside those desks are single companies (Germany 4, UK 4, Israel 3, China 2, Netherlands 2, Singapore 2, and one each in Malaysia, Sweden, Brazil, Japan, France, Finland, Italy).

investment_scope.basis: DERIVED from the grind's own focus column, not from any site vocabulary (the firm's 2001-2009 sector pages describe a book that ended fifteen years ago). Ten values clear the 10-company floor (~4.5% of 284); Climate & Energy (4) and Crypto & Web3 (1) fall below it and are not published. 19 rows sit outside the taxonomy and are reported as such rather than force-fitted.

investment_range.basis: Built from the 25 CITED entry rounds of the pre-registered stage key rather than from Form D bands, which this run demoted (R4, 7/16 on the gate). Lower limit $3.5M: New Relic's 2008 first round, the smallest documented entry. Median $13.5M: the midpoint of the cited entry rounds (Snapchat's $13.5M Series A sits on it; Uber $11M, Elasticsearch $10M, Instagram $7M, Amplitude $9M, Confluent $6.9M below; Optimizely $28M, Cerebras $27M, Airbyte $26M, Hipcamp $25M above). Upper limit $225M: the two AI Infrastructure vehicles Benchmark raised in February 2026 to put ~$225M into one Cerebras round — the largest single position the firm has ever taken, and now the visible ceiling given the $1.25B growth fund. A round size is a proxy for check size and is fair here because Benchmark leads and takes a board seat in nearly every entry.

history.value: Benchmark was founded in Menlo Park in 1995 by Bob Kagle, Bruce Dunlevie, Andy Rachleff, Kevin Harvey and Val Vaden as a partnership of equals. Its early bets on eBay, Uber, Snapchat, Instagram, Twitter and Discord made it one of the best-known firms in Silicon Valley. After two decades of roughly $425M funds, it raised $2B in 2026, including its first growth fund.
history.basis: Assembled from the sources cited across this sidecar plus the run's own evidence: the fund ladder from Form D, the desk history from the archived site and the 2007 Balderton and Benchmark Israel VC 2007 separations, the 2026 fund raises from TechCrunch (2026-02-06 and 2026-06-03), and the base's own shape. Rewritten to the reader-facing shape (PRO-147, 2026-09-24). Not counted in the portfolio: the London desk (2000, became Balderton Capital in 2007) and the Israeli desk (2001, Benchmark Israel VC 2007 Ltd). The deal sizes behind the eBay, Uber, Instagram, Snapchat and Elasticsearch entries, and the 2026 Cerebras vehicles, are in the basis above.

investment_concept.value: Benchmark backs founders at their first institutional round, usually a Series A, and takes a board seat, investing as one equal partnership.
investment_concept.basis: Derived, flagged: the firm publishes no statement (its site is a wordmark and two addresses, read 2026-09-26). The line rests on the equal-partnership structure the firm has described in interviews and on its first-institutional-round, board-seat pattern (mostly Series A entries). PRO-147: the thesis is the firm's own crisp statement (Erik, 2026-09-26); this is the one exception.
